registered: see the git commit that added this file (2026-10-05): during the v2 campaign's first training, before any run of the corrected network
class: controlled experiment on corpus-v2 VAL (TEST untouched); one factor: how the network is built

finding_that_motivates_it.what: every AeroTrack detector so far (repair series, generalization series, v2 campaign; planned v3 / X1 / C2) was built from YAMLs with flat multipliers and no scale letter; Ultralytics 8.4.115 then resolves scale = '' and parse_model's `if scale in "mlx"` is True for the empty string, so every C3k2 block is built with c3k=True (the YOLO11 m/l/x block with an inner C3k) instead of YOLO11n's Bottleneck
finding_that_motivates_it.consequence: the network is not YOLO11n (2.613 M params) and only 417 / 649 tensors (64.3 %) of yolo11n.pt (trained with Ultralytics 8.2.100) load into it; the C3k2 internals of layers 2, 4, 13, 16, 19 start from random init. The earlier diagnosis ('C3k2 cv1 convs are 1x1 in 8.4.115 vs 3x3 in the checkpoint') described a symptom; src/model/aerotrack_trainer.transfer_pretrained's docstring ('the C3k2 blocks ... transfer') and the v2 registration's 'starts as COCO YOLO11n on frame t' are therefore inaccurate (erratum: experiments/aerotrack_v2/ERRATUM_architecture.md)
finding_that_motivates_it.what_stays_valid: every registered comparison so far is between arms built the same way (same mis-built architecture, identical starting weights apart from zeroed neighbour channels), so window / SPD / recipe verdicts are internally valid; absolute accuracy may be below what the intended network reaches
finding_that_motivates_it.fix: src/model/yolo11-stride-std.yaml = yolo11-stride.yaml with `scales: {n: [0.50, 0.25, 1024]}` -> C3k2(c3k=False): 2.591 M params, 448 / 499 tensors (89.8 %) load (the rest: 2-class head internals); function-preserving init exact (max |diff| 0.0)

arms.as_built: the v2 campaign's runs of the configuration it selects: v2_<cfg>_s0_e20, v2_<cfg>_s1_e20 (shared; no new training)
arms.standard: v3 model 'n_std' (src/model/yolo11-stride-std.yaml, COCO yolo11n.pt + centre-frame stem, gen_lib function-preserving init) with the same window: v3_n_std__<window>_s0_e20, _s1_e20
arms.window: from experiments/aerotrack_v2/reports/v2_decisions.json selected_candidate (causal_g4 -> causal_g4, sym_g4 -> sym_g4, stock -> ttt); decided by v2's rule, not here

held_fixed: the v2 recipe, corpus v2, seeds 0 / 1, monitoring, evaluation protocol and frame set, checkpoint = last.pt
primary_metric: CST drone AP50 on corpus-v2 VAL (as v2)
rule: the v2 superiority rule with the v2 margins: seed-mean delta (standard - as_built) > 0.02; delta > 0 for every seed; paired dataset-stratified sequence bootstrap 95 % CI excludes 0 (B = 1000); seed-mean Anti-UAV delta > -0.02. Futility: if the seed-0 CST delta <= 0, seed 1 is not trained and F1 is NOT SUPPORTED.

downstream_adoption.if_SUPPORTED: X1 trains n_std (amended in its registration before it runs); CF's detector uses n_std (an n_std run of C2's selected window is trained before CF if that window differs); C2 stays on the as-built network (a relative window study sharing v2's runs) and says so
downstream_adoption.if_NOT_SUPPORTED: everything stays on the as-built network; the erratum stands as documentation

component_gate.measured_failure: 35.7 % of the pretrained tensors never loaded (random init) because of the parser's empty-scale branch
component_gate.why: with 20 epochs x 25,000 samples, features that start from COCO are likely better on tiny / low-contrast targets than random C3k blocks
component_gate.baseline: the as-built network (v2's own runs, same seeds)
component_gate.novelty: none (a correctness fix); its value is the measured size of the effect
component_gate.cost: -0.022 M params; identical FLOPs class; no runtime change
component_gate.isolating_ablation: only the C3k2 inner block (and hence the transferable fraction) changes
component_gate.falsifier: seed-mean delta <= 0.02 or a non-positive seed

queue: after the causal-detector caches, before X1 (whose network depends on this verdict)
